goal.text: MiHa is a reference-grade browser agent harness: its budget, its laws and its document graph are all machine-checked, and every claim below is proven with a negative control
goal.reason: The aim now covers the implementation and its budgets, not only the decision record

claims.text: Every relative document link and every ADR supersedes target in the decision record resolves to a file that exists, and the supersedes chain terminates without looping

review.reason: Owner re-read the decision: the layer diagram no longer names a protocol layer that the tree does not have, and the diagram is now checked against the tree

claims.falsifier: A document links to a file that does not exist, or an ADR names a missing or looping supersedes target

claims.text: Every decision label referenced anywhere in the documentation is defined by an ADR heading, each ADR's labels are contiguous from D1, and no ADR defines decisions that nothing else references

review.reason: Owner re-read the decision: the layer diagram was corrected to match the tree, and the layer agreement is now checked by a machine

claims.text: The event stream satisfies laws S1 to S7 as written in ADR 0004 D22: events arrive in push order exactly once, result resolves once with the terminal value, late events are ignored, iteration ends after the terminal event, nothing is lost between a push and the start of iteration, a failure ends iteration by throwing and rejects result, and a close without a terminal event rejects result and ends iteration

review.reason: Owner re-read the decision: the law set now states the dialect's admission set, adds S6 and S7, and every law carries its derivation. The texts of the claims were narrowed to what is actually enforced, so that a claim can be falsified

claims.falsifier: A law is broken: order or count of delivered events changes, result resolves with the wrong value or more than once, a late event is delivered, or an event pushed before iteration is lost
claims.control: sed -i 's/this.#buffer.shift() as T/this.#buffer.pop() as T/' src/core/event-stream.ts

claims.text: The tool-parameter dialect satisfies laws C1 to C3 as written in ADR 0004 D22: every value the dialect admits is accepted, every value it does not admit is rejected with an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer path, and coercion happens only where the dialect says so. The admission set is the table in the decision, not the implementation

review.reason: Owner re-read the decision: the law set now states the dialect's admission set, adds S6 and S7, and every law carries its derivation. The texts of the claims were narrowed to what is actually enforced, so that a claim can be falsified

claims.falsifier: A value the dialect admits is rejected, a rejected value carries no path, or a value is coerced where the dialect did not ask for coercion
claims.control: sed -i 's/} else if (schema.coerce \&\& typeof value === "string") {/} else if (typeof value === "string") {/' src/schema/dialect.ts

claims.text: The dispatch planner satisfies laws M1, M2 and M3 and policy T1: every call of a batch appears exactly once across the plan and the rejections, a call whose arguments did not arrive complete is never planned for execution, a failed tool is a result carrying isError rather than ordinary content, and an exclusive tool runs alone while shared tools around it still share a group
claims.falsifier: A call is planned and rejected at once or neither, a call with unparseable arguments reaches a group, a failure is reported as ordinary content, or an exclusive tool shares a group with another exclusive tool

claims.text: The state machine and the driver keep laws M1 to M4 and T4 over a whole run: every tool call of every batch receives exactly one result -- including on rejection, tool failure, truncation, provider error and cancellation -- the results are recorded in assistant order, a failed tool is a result carrying isError, a provider failure is an event that leaves every streamed call answered, and an aborted signal ends the run at the next boundary with every in-flight call answered
claims.falsifier: A call is left unanswered on any path, a call with unparseable arguments reaches a group, a failure becomes ordinary content or a thrown error, or the results are recorded in completion order
claims.control: sed -i 's/const flushed = flushResults({ ...state, results }, outputs);/const flushed = { ...state, phase: "settling" as const, results: [] };/' src/core/run.ts

claims.text: The commit gate runs every check that needs only bun — the budget, the documents and the tests — and all of them pass
claims.falsifier: One of the checks is not run by the gate, or one of them fails. The type check is deliberately not claimed: the isolated evidence copy is a git clone with no node_modules, so a control there would fail for a reason unrelated to its subject, and the method counts an infrastructure failure as no refutation at all

claims.text: The provider adapter never throws and never rejects: a network failure, a refusal, a malformed chunk, a tool call without a stream index, any exception raised while reading the provider's body, and a stream that ends without a terminal event all arrive at the core as an error event, so the core's pairing invariant survives a broken provider

review.reason: ADR 0005 touched only by two cross-reference sentences (D44 seam pointer, D47/D48 finalisation notes); the provider protocol law is unchanged; re-read the diff before recording

claims.falsifier: The adapter raises, or a stream that ends without a terminal event leaves the core waiting instead of receiving an error

claims.text: Every fragment of a tool call's arguments reaches the core in order and attached to the right call: parallel calls are correlated by their stream index, the arguments of each call concatenate to exactly what the provider sent, a call whose id arrives late still starts once and carries every fragment, and a call without a stream index is refused rather than merged into another call

review.reason: ADR 0005 touch is a cross-reference sentence only; the arguments-intact law and its falsifier are unchanged; re-read the diff before recording

claims.falsifier: A fragment is lost, reordered, attached to the wrong call, or a call starts twice

claims.text: The layers named in the architectural decision are exactly the layers the source tree has, and every one of them has a declared budget
claims.falsifier: The decision names a layer the tree does not have, the tree has a layer the decision does not name, or a layer has no budget
claims.control: sed -i 's|^core/        the message|core\/        the message\nmisc\/        a layer nobody budgeted|' docs/adr/0002-core-harness.md

claims.text: The capability bridge is a closed set: only a capability that is an **own** entry of the host's table is reachable, a name inherited from Object.prototype is not registered and is refused by name, and the caller is told which capability was refused
claims.falsifier: A capability the host did not register can be called, or the caller is not told which capability was refused

claims.text: A capability that fails rejects the caller with an Error whose message is **exactly** the failure's message: error.message for an Error, String(value) otherwise, and a capability failure and a carrying failure stay distinguishable from each other
claims.falsifier: A failing capability resolves instead of rejecting, or the caller is told something other than what failed

claims.text: Every capability call is answered exactly once, and the answer reaches the caller that asked: two concurrent calls never receive each other's answers, and an answer whose id matches no pending call is discarded rather than given to another caller
claims.falsifier: An answer reaches the wrong caller, an answer is delivered twice, or a call is never answered
claims.control: sed -i 's/const pending = byId.get(frame.id);/const pending = byId.values().next().value;/' src/worker/bridge.ts

claims.text: A value the channel cannot carry fails the call with an error, in both directions: arguments that cannot be sent and a result that cannot be sent. Neither replaces the other, and the caller is never left waiting for an answer that cannot arrive
claims.falsifier: An argument or a result that the channel refuses leaves the caller waiting, or the failure is reported as something other than a carrying failure
claims.control: sed -i 's/"the arguments cannot be sent"/"the call failed"/' src/worker/bridge.ts

claims.text: Every capability call that reaches the host is answered exactly once: a call that succeeded, one that failed and one that was refused each produce a single answer, and no answer is sent for a call that was never made
claims.falsifier: A call receives two answers, or a call receives none
claims.control: sed -i 's/if (tryPost(port, frame)) return;/if (tryPost(port, frame)) { port.post(frame); return; }/' src/worker/bridge.ts

claims.text: The worker host hands the bridge the application's capability table and nothing else, so the set of capability names the worker can reach is exactly the set of own keys of that table. It passes every event frame it receives to onEvent, unchanged and in arrival order. After terminate() returns it posts no further frame to the worker, including an answer to a call that was in flight. It never lets an exception from the worker, a capability or the channel escape into the application's thread; an exception raised by the application's own onEvent callback is the application's, and propagates
claims.falsifier: The worker reaches a capability the host did not register, an event arrives out of order or not at all, a call that arrives after the realm ended is answered, or the host raises out of a broken worker

claims.text: The delegating side sends exactly one offer, carrying the protocol version, the task id, the task and the context, and nothing else: the delegator's tools are never reachable by the peer. It forwards every event the peer sends for that task, in arrival order, and ignores frames for another task and frames it does not know. The task resolves with the peer's outcome verbatim, a refusal resolves as a failure whose error is the peer's reason, and cancelling posts a cancel frame
claims.falsifier: The offer carries the delegator's tools, a peer's call to one of them is answered, an event arrives out of order or is dropped, a refusal loses its reason, or the outcome never resolves

claims.text: The driver asks the host's async approve seam before each tool runs: a denial becomes an error tool result the model reads while the tool never runs, a rewrite is re-validated and only a valid one reaches the tool, the host sees the call, the tool and the already-validated arguments, and with no seam every planned tool runs
claims.falsifier: a planned tool executing before the host answers, a denial leaving its call without exactly one error result, or an unvalidated rewrite reaching the tool
